findings.description: CONTRIBUTING.md claims the automated review 'does not run on external pull requests,' but the workflow is actor-gated, not PR-author-gated, and its issue_comment trigger fires on any PR when the owner comments `@claude review`.
findings.body:
This line says:

> An automated review runs on pull requests opened by the repository owner and posts inline findings. It does not run on external pull requests, so those get a human review instead; expect questions grounded in the decisions log.

This overstates the boundary. `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` (lines 34-38) gates on the *actor*, not the PR's author:

```yaml
if: |
  github.actor == github.repository_owner && (
    (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.draft == false) ||
    (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude review'))
  )
```

The workflow's own comment (lines 31-33) confirms this is intentional: "Owner-only: the review bills the owner's Claude subscription, so a PR opened, pushed to, or `@claude review`-commented by anyone else is skipped. `actor` is the PR opener/pusher or the commenter." Nothing in the workflow checks `github.event.pull_request.user.login` (the PR's actual author). So if the repository owner comments `@claude review` on an externally-opened PR, the job condition evaluates true and the automated review runs and posts inline findings on it — contradicting the blanket claim that it never runs on external PRs.

Suggest rephrasing to something like: "An automated review runs automatically when the repository owner opens, pushes to, or marks a PR ready; on any other PR (including external ones) the owner can trigger it manually by commenting `@claude review`. Otherwise expect a human review, grounded in the decisions log."

findings.description: "The pre-commit hook runs the test suite" undersells what it actually gates: `scripts/pre-commit` also runs lint (Biome) and typecheck before the tests, so a contributor could be surprised when a commit is blocked with no test failure involved.
findings.suggestion: The pre-commit hook lints, typechecks, and runs the test suite before every commit.

findings.description: Same undersell as CONTRIBUTING.md#L22: "the pre-commit hook you install once runs the tests before every commit" omits that it also lints and typechecks.
findings.suggestion: ...and the pre-commit hook you install once lints, typechecks, and tests before every commit.

findings.description: "The full role list is in `.claude/project.env`" points readers at a single regex alternation instead of `docs/conventions/naming.md`'s explicit, human-readable "25 valid roles" section that the paragraph above already links to.
findings.suggestion: The full role list is in [`docs/conventions/naming.md`](docs/conventions/naming.md#the-25-valid-roles).

findings.description: The module-boundaries bullet adds "`src/adapters/` holds the per-language toolchains" alongside the two boundary rules AGENTS.md actually documents (`src/cli/` thin, `src/claude/` sole Claude Code touchpoint); `src/adapters/` isn't named as a boundary rule anywhere in AGENTS.md or docs/conventions, so it's presented with more authority than it has.

"A guard needs a test that fails when the guard is removed" is stated as a general Code-section rule, but docs/conventions/testing.md never states this as a blanket obligation — the "fails when the guard is deleted" phrasing only appears describing specific historical decisions in docs/09-decisions.md.

"The gate flags diffs over 600 changed lines... fine, but say so" undersells decision 17: an oversize diff is mechanically refused unless `--accept-debt "<reason>" --review-by "<condition>"` is passed (docs/09-decisions.md lines ~379-382), not just mentioned in the PR body.
